# YANG test fixture manifest

Checked-in YANG fixtures used by `tests/yang_catalogue.rs`. All content is
redistributable: OpenConfig models are Apache-2.0; IETF RFC modules are
published under the IETF Trust / RFC Editor trust provisions.

## Synthetic fixtures (`*.yang` at this directory root)

`test-base.yang`, `test-sub.yang` (submodule), `test-aug.yang`,
`test-deviated.yang`, `test-broken.yang` — hand-written, authored for this
repository. They exercise augments, deviations, features, submodules,
multi-key lists, typedefs, units and failure diagnostics.

## Independent reference oracle

`reference/expected-schema.json` is generated by
`scripts/yang_reference.py` using **pyang** (`pyang -f tree`) — a
development/test oracle only, never a Bonsai runtime dependency.

Regenerate (requires pyang, e.g. `pip install pyang`):

```sh
python3 scripts/yang_reference.py --pyang /path/to/pyang \
    --out tests/fixtures/yang/reference/expected-schema.json
```

The JSON embeds the pyang version, the exact command and per-file SHA-256
checksums so drift is detectable. The Rust suite compares Bonsai's compiled
path index against this reference per module (path, kind, config,
mandatory, keys, status) and fails on any missing/extra/mismatched entry.

Modules producing zero data paths (`openconfig-types`,
`openconfig-yang-types`, `openconfig-extensions`,
`openconfig-platform-types`, `openconfig-transport-types`,
`ietf-yang-types`, `ietf-inet-types`) contain only typedefs, identities,
groupings and features — pyang emits no `module:` tree section for them
either, which the test verifies.
